svg.title: Async-RBench: key evaluation mechanisms
svg.desc: The same participant-safe task and benchmark-owned concurrent initial workstreams enter independent Linear and Async routes. A, B and C are illustrative independent subagents, not a fixed model pool or required count. Private event rules define affected and preserved work across eight themes without exposing scoring truth. Linear waits for all terminal child states before showing one stable result batch to the main agent. Async uses a shared qualitative time axis. Main work overlaps all three children and continues across A completion. A produces a result first. A continuous amber path runs from A through the compact Result delivery gate to the later actual-presentation point on Main. Public check means public submission-contract validation. Rules and queue cover event policy, possible staging, release and waiting until the result is included in a launched main-model request. The upward Async interrupt arrow ends exactly where Main changes from Working to Handle message. It denotes a new visible message changing subsequent work, not cancellation of an in-flight API request. Main then Continues and sends later Control down to still-running B; the control line passes only through the empty time after A has ended. C continues independently. Main, B and C extend beyond the displayed fragment. Time has no units and is not measured or to scale. Update and Keep may happen together. Run records represent whole-execution delivery, actual presentation, agent actions and event-boundary artifact digests; hidden checks never gate public delivery. BTS arrows denote eventual whole-run final states. DRS comes from independent whole-execution evidence and private checks, half process and half event outcome, without strict attribution to one response window. Metrics aggregate independently through repetitions and tasks to equal-weight theme means, with coverage reported separately.
